Paths under `src/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`, `ci/` and the rest of"},{"id":"p4s4","text":" `docs/` exist in the repository and are **not published** — this file names them as coordinates, no"},{"id":"p4s5","text":"t as files you can open from the tarball."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"English · 中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Deutsch · Español · Português · Русский · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français"},{"id":"p5s2","text":" · Deutsch · Español · Português · Русский"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"Add a WSL workspace from the DeepSeek Harness web GUI and run the whole agent session — bash command"},{"id":"p6s2","text":"s and file reads/writes — inside a local WSL distribution with Linux paths. Nothing needs to be inst"},{"id":"p6s3","text":"alled inside WSL. The session can reach both WSL and Windows at the same time: bash commands run ins"},{"id":"p6s4","text":"ide the WSL distribution, while Windows files stay accessible via `/mnt/<drive>` (for example `/mnt/"},{"id":"p6s5","text":"stribution, while Windows files stay accessible via `/mnt/<drive>` (for example `/mnt/c/Users/...`)."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"## Install"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"Pick one of the three ways below, then restart `dsh web`:"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"After restarting `dsh web`, a W button appears in the Workspaces section header, immediately right o"},{"id":"p10s2","text":"f the add-workspace control; the collapsed rail keeps it beside Settings at the sidebar foot."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"## Compatibility"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"This build declares these DSH releases, each verified on an isolated instance (its own `DSH_HOME`, d"},{"id":"p12s2","text":"ependencies pinned to that release, the full check suite):"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"`0.1.0-rc.7` · `0.1.0-rc.8` · `0.1.1-rc.1` · `0.1.1-rc.2` · `0.1.2-rc.1` · `0.1.3-alpha.2` · `0.1.5-"},{"id":"p13s2","text":"rc.1` · `0.1.5-rc.2` · `0.1.7-rc.1` · `0.1.7-rc.2` · `0.2.0-rc.2` · `0.2.1-rc.2`"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"The list mirrors `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases` in `package.json`, and a unit test fails if the two"},{"id":"p14s2","text":" drift apart. `0.2.1-rc.2` is the DSH release DSH Desktop `0.2.1-rc.2` ships — verified against the "},{"id":"p14s3","text":"host inside that application's own bundle, not only against the npm release — so the Desktop is cove"},{"id":"p14s4","text":"red by the same declaration; the app's help panel (the dialog's \"?\" button) shows the same chips nex"},{"id":"p14s5","text":"t to the plugin version. The plugin detects the DSH generation at runtime and picks the matching API"},{"id":"p14s6","text":", and a release exposing neither fails loudly instead of leaving an empty workspace. A release outsi"},{"id":"p14s7","text":"de the list usually still works, but is unverified."},{"id":"p15s1","text":"## Usage"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"Click that W button — or pick “Add WSL workspace”, directly under “Add workspace…” in the same contr"},{"id":"p16s2","text":"ol’s menu — to open the \"Add WSL workspace\" dialog. Pick a distribution from the list, then browse t"},{"id":"p16s3","text":"he directory tree or type an absolute Linux path (for example `/home/me/proj`) — use the Check butto"},{"id":"p16s4","text":"n to verify the path exists before creating the workspace. The dialog follows the DeepSeek Harness U"},{"id":"p16s5","text":"I language. The username field is optional: leave it empty to run commands as the distribution's def"},{"id":"p16s6","text":"ault user, or name a Linux user of that distribution to run the session as that user instead (equiva"},{"id":"p16s7","text":"lent to `wsl.exe -u <username>`). The username only changes the bash tool's run identity — the file "},{"id":"p16s8","text":"tools go through the Windows-side WSL share and are unaffected. Each workspace's username is kept in"},{"id":"p16s9","text":" `<dshHome>/wsl-workspaces.json`; delete the entry (or recreate the workspace from the dialog) to re"},{"id":"p16s10","text":"turn to the default user."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"Click \"Create & open\" to start a new session in the workspace. In the new session the bash tool exec"},{"id":"p17s2","text":"utes commands inside the chosen distribution and `read`/`write`/`edit` operate on WSL files, so ever"},{"id":"p17s3","text":"y path the model sees is a Linux path. The mode picker keeps working as usual: Standard, PTC, Minima"},{"id":"p17s4","text":"l and Creative each land on their WSL variant automatically (the WSL variant entries in the picker a"},{"id":"p17s5","text":"re bilingual, e.g. `WSL · Standard mode（标准模式）`), and Windows files stay reachable from inside the se"},{"id":"p17s6","text":"ssion under `/mnt/<drive>` (for example `/mnt/c/Users/...`). The dialog's \"?\" button opens a panel w"},{"id":"p17s7","text":"ith the DSH releases this build declares, how the plugin is used, and the limitations it cannot fix."},{"id":"p18s1","text":"## Behavior notes"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"- **bash tool**: runs inside the WSL distribution as the configured username (empty = the distro def"},{"id":"p19s2","text":"ault user, often `root`), so it can read and write anywhere in the distro. The Windows ACL sandbox c"},{"id":"p19s3","text":"annot wrap `wsl.exe` — its children run on the Linux kernel side — so WSL itself is the isolation bo"},{"id":"p19s4","text":"undary and the DSH file policy does not apply to bash.\n- **File tools (`read`/`write`/`edit`)**: go "},{"id":"p19s5","text":"through the Windows-side WSL 9P share; the username field does not affect them. Two seams the host's"},{"id":"p19s6","text":" own provider would supply are re-established inside the WSL world, because a variant mounts this pl"},{"id":"p19s7","text":"ugin's `fs` provider in the preset's isolate realm where the host's `fs-sandbox` wrapper is not in t"},{"id":"p19s8","text":"he call path. **Symlinks**: the share lists a Linux link but cannot resolve it, so a link path used "},{"id":"p19s9","text":"to look like a missing file; `resolve`/`lstat` now ask the distribution (`wsl.exe … readlink -f`) an"},{"id":"p19s10","text":"d continue at the real path, and a link is never replaced by a regular file. **The access mode**: `w"},{"id":"p19s11","text":"rite`/`edit` are fenced by `ctx.sandboxPolicy` exactly as the host backend fences them — the same `w"},{"id":"p19s12","text":"ritableRoots` allow-list (plus the distribution's `/tmp`, the temp area of the world the session run"},{"id":"p19s13","text":"s in), the same `FS_SANDBOX_DENIED` the tool layer renders as a denial, and the same `sandboxMode` f"},{"id":"p19s14","text":"act it reads for escalation. Because the fence runs after resolution it judges the real path: a link"},{"id":"p19s15","text":" out of the workspace is an outside write and is denied under `workspace-write`. A deployment that m"},{"id":"p19s16","text":"ounts no policy service fences nothing, as on the host. [长行截断]\n[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"## Driving it from another agent"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"[该节后续省略]"}],"truncated":true}
